UK provisional peak of 37.7C shatters previous record by huge margin, while Germany hits all-time high of 41.7C Last week’s heatwave across western Europe shattered national June records and set new all-time highs. The UK recorded a provisional high of 37.7C at Lingwood in Norfolk on Friday 27 June, smashing the previous June record of 35.6C, set in 1976. Such a margin is exceptionally rare: temperature records are typically broken by 0.1C or 0.2C, not a remarkable 2.1C. Germany reached 41.7C in Coschen on 28 of June, breaking its all-time record for a third consecutive day. The Netherlands set a new June record with 39.4C on 26 June, while Hungary recorded an all-time high of 42C in Szécsény on 30 June.

Alongside the daytime extremes, much of Europe experienced widespread tropical nights, when overnight temperatures do not fall below 20C. The highest minimum temperature recorded during this period was 29.4C in East Saxony, Germany. France also endured several days above 40C, forcing some nuclear power plants shutting down. This week, north-western China is experiencing similarly hot conditions. Temperatures reached 45C on Monday and 47C on Tuesday, with the heatwave expected to continue until 7 July. Extreme heat warnings have been issued in the Yuli and Ruoqiang regions, where temperatures are expected to exceed 45C all week. Parts of Ruoqiang, Qiemo, Korla, Luntai and the Yanqi Basin are expected to top 40C.

Europe is in the midst of its second big heat wave of the year, and it’s breaking more records. France just recorded its hottest day ever, with temperatures exceeding 44 degrees Celsius in some places. Around 40 people have drowned in local water bodies, likely attempting to escape the heat, and thousands more are without electricity. As temperatures hit a sweltering 36 degrees in some regions of the United Kingdom, schools canceled classes and train delays abounded. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres described London as “cooking.” As the city hosts its annual Climate Action Week, the U.K. meteorological service has issued a red alert for multiple regions, signalling that exceptionally hot and humid weather is forecasted and likely to impact the general public. Switzerland and Spain have also issued warnings to residents.

[Lähde: The Guardian World]
UK provisional peak of 37.7C shatters previous record by huge margin, while Germany hits all-time high of 41.7C

Last week’s heatwave across western Europe shattered national June records and set new all-time highs.

The UK recorded a provisional high of 37.7C at Lingwood in Norfolk on Friday 27 June, smashing the previous June record of 35.6C, set in 1976. Such a margin is exceptionally rare: temperature records are typically broken by 0.1C or 0.2C, not a remarkable 2.1C.

Germany reached 41.7C in Coschen on 28 of June, breaking its all-time record for a third consecutive day. The Netherlands set a new June record with 39.4C on 26 June, while Hungary recorded an all-time high of 42C in Szécsény on 30 June.

Alongside the daytime extremes, much of Europe experienced widespread tropical nights, when overnight temperatures do not fall below 20C. The highest minimum temperature recorded during this period was 29.4C in East Saxony, Germany. France also endured several days above 40C, forcing some nuclear power plants shutting down.

This week, north-western China is experiencing similarly hot conditions. Temperatures reached 45C on Monday and 47C on Tuesday, with the heatwave expected to continue until 7 July. Extreme heat warnings have been issued in the Yuli and Ruoqiang regions, where temperatures are expected to exceed 45C all week. Parts of Ruoqiang, Qiemo, Korla, Luntai and the Yanqi Basin are expected to top 40C.

The heatwave is being driven by a persistent high-pressure system over the continent, which is drawing in hot, dry air while blocking cooler air masses. In such an arid region, the lack of soil moisture limits evaporative cooling, causing the ground and air to heat even more rapidly.

Authorities have urged residents and businesses to avoid outdoor manual work during the hottest parts of the day, protect elderly and vulnerable people, and take extra precautions against wildfires.

Road surface temperatures are forecast to exceed 60C, increasing the risk of asphalt deformation and disruption on highways. Such temperatures heighten the likelihood of breakdowns and cargo spoilages. Railways have also introduced speed restrictions because of high track temperatures.

payload.title: Helleaalto rikkoi kesäkuun lämpöennätyksiä eri puolilla Eurooppaa
payload.summary: Länsi-Euroopan viime viikon helleaalto rikkoi kesäkuun lämpöennätyksiä Britanniassa ja Alankomaissa sekä kaikkien aikojen lämpöennätyksiä Saksassa ja Unkarissa.
payload.content:
Länsi-Euroopan viime viikon helleaalto rikkoi useita kansallisia lämpöennätyksiä ja toi poikkeuksellisen korkeita lukemia myös yöaikaan. Britanniassa mitattiin alustavasti 37,7 astetta Lingwoodissa Norfolkissa perjantaina 27. kesäkuuta, mikä ylitti maan aiemman kesäkuun ennätyksen selvästi.

## Britannian ennätys ylittyi harvinaisen suurella erolla

Britannian aiempi kesäkuun lämpöennätys oli 35,6 astetta vuodelta 1976. Uusi alustava lukema olisi siis 2,1 astetta korkeampi. Lämpöennätykset rikkoutuvat yleensä vain asteen kymmenyksillä, joten ero on poikkeuksellisen suuri.

Saksassa mitattiin 41,7 astetta Coschenissa 28. kesäkuuta. Lukema rikkoi maan kaikkien aikojen lämpöennätyksen jo kolmantena peräkkäisenä päivänä. Alankomaissa kesäkuun ennätys nousi 39,4 asteeseen 26. kesäkuuta, ja Unkarissa mitattiin kaikkien aikojen ennätys, 42 astetta, Szécsényssä 30. kesäkuuta.

## Kuumuus jatkui myös öisin

Päivälämpötilojen lisäksi suuri osa Eurooppaa koki niin sanottuja trooppisia öitä, jolloin lämpötila ei laske alle 20 asteen. Jakson korkein alin lämpötila oli 29,4 astetta Itä-Saksin alueella Saksassa.

Ranskassa lämpötila pysyi useina päivinä yli 40 asteessa. Kuumuus pakotti myös joitakin ydinvoimaloita pysäyttämään toimintaansa. Toisen lähteen mukaan Ranskassa mitattiin maan kuumin päivä, ja joissakin paikoissa lämpötila ylitti 44 astetta. Lisäksi noin 40 ihmisen kerrottiin hukkuneen paikallisiin vesistöihin, todennäköisesti hakeuduttuaan veteen kuumuutta pakoon, ja tuhannet olivat ilman sähköä.

Britanniassa kuumuus vaikutti arkeen myös muualla: osassa maata lämpötila nousi 36 asteeseen, kouluja suljettiin ja junaliikenteessä oli viivästyksiä. Britannian meteorologinen palvelu antoi useille alueille punaisen varoituksen poikkeuksellisen kuumasta ja kosteasta säästä. Myös Sveitsi ja Espanja varoittivat asukkaitaan helteestä.

## Samankaltaista kuumuutta Kiinassa

Euroopan hellejakson jälkeen samankaltaisia oloja koettiin Luoteis-Kiinassa. Lämpötila nousi maanantaina 45 asteeseen ja tiistaina 47 asteeseen, ja helleaallon arvioitiin jatkuvan 7. heinäkuuta asti. Yulin ja Ruoqiangin alueille annettiin äärimmäisen kuumuuden varoituksia, ja useilla alueilla lämpötilojen odotettiin pysyvän yli 40 asteessa.
summary_bullets: Britanniassa mitattiin alustavasti 37,7 astetta, mikä ylitti maan kesäkuun ennätyksen 2,1 asteella.
Saksa, Alankomaat ja Unkari kirjasivat uusia lämpöennätyksiä kesäkuun lopulla.
Kuumuus vaikutti myös yöaikaan, liikenteeseen, kouluihin ja energiantuotantoon.

UK provisional peak of 37.7C shatters previous record by huge margin, while Germany hits all-time high of 41.7C Last week’s heatwave across western Europe shattered national June records and set new all-time highs. The UK recorded a provisional high of 37.7C at Lingwood in Norfolk on Friday 27 June, smashing the previous June record of 35.6C, set in 1976. Such a margin is exceptionally rare: temperature records are typically broken by 0.1C or 0.2C, not a remarkable 2.1C. Germany reached 41.7C in Coschen on 28 of June, breaking its all-time record for a third consecutive day. The Netherlands set a new June record with 39.4C on 26 June, while Hungary recorded an all-time high of 42C in Szécsény on 30 June.

Alongside the daytime extremes, much of Europe experienced widespread tropical nights, when overnight temperatures do not fall below 20C. The highest minimum temperature recorded during this period was 29.4C in East Saxony, Germany. France also endured several days above 40C, forcing some nuclear power plants shutting down. This week, north-western China is experiencing similarly hot conditions. Temperatures reached 45C on Monday and 47C on Tuesday, with the heatwave expected to continue until 7 July. Extreme heat warnings have been issued in the Yuli and Ruoqiang regions, where temperatures are expected to exceed 45C all week. Parts of Ruoqiang, Qiemo, Korla, Luntai and the Yanqi Basin are expected to top 40C.

Europe is in the midst of its second big heat wave of the year, and it’s breaking more records. France just recorded its hottest day ever, with temperatures exceeding 44 degrees Celsius in some places. Around 40 people have drowned in local water bodies, likely attempting to escape the heat, and thousands more are without electricity. As temperatures hit a sweltering 36 degrees in some regions of the United Kingdom, schools canceled classes and train delays abounded. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres described London as “cooking.” As the city hosts its annual Climate Action Week, the U.K. meteorological service has issued a red alert for multiple regions, signalling that exceptionally hot and humid weather is forecasted and likely to impact the general public. Switzerland and Spain have also issued warnings to residents.
